question: How do I automate the publishing of my documentation using GitHub Actions?
ground_truth: To automate documentation publishing with GitHub Actions, you need to: 1) Generate a token using `fern token` command, 2) Add this token as a repository secret called `FERN_TOKEN`, and 3) Create a GitHub Actions workflow that runs on pushes to the main branch and executes `fern generate --docs` with the token as an environment variable.

metadata.cited_context:
### Usage in GitHub Actions
To automate the publishing process, you can use a GitHub Action workflow to publish your docs when a push is made to the `main` branch. 

<Steps>
<Step title="Generate token">

Use `fern token` to generate a token for authenticating the Fern CLI in CI/CD environments. The token is specific to your organization defined in [`fern.config.json`](/learn/sdks/overview/project-structure#fernconfigjson) and doesn't expire.

<CodeBlock title="terminal">
```bash
fern token
```
</CodeBlock>
</Step>
<Step title="Add token as a secret">
Add the token as a [repository secret](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/using-secrets-in-github-actions#creating-secrets-for-a-repository) called `FERN_TOKEN`.
</Step>
<Step title="Create workflow">
Create a Publish Docs workflow ([example](https://github.com/fern-api/docs/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish-docs.yml)), and reference the secret.
